original_card.question: Can the proposed P104 joint endpoint flags be realized by a chronological correction program with coefficients, dirty restoration and an affordable complete bill?
methods: Construct one side-correction word at an explicit chronological cut with the needed frames still available.
Derive a lower bound on the side correction and hosting costs that decides whether this channel can beat the selected budget.
original_card.acceptance_gate: An exact arbitrary-input identity, source/target frame availability and restoration at the chosen cut, plus the complete channel+correction+idle/hosting bill or an explicit favorable bound. The native channel alone is not a supplier. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read the revision-6 family record and #2981 static joint flags, alongside the reviewed #1991 channel. #2981 is an author-checked source archive, not an independently validated executable correction or a refutation of program-level lifetime floors.
first_step.scope: Source-bound orientation only. Read the named package and review before relying on its local evidence; this command is not its replay or supplier admission.

original_card.first_experiment: After checking live handoffs, pin one named collection from #2981 and attach acquisition/delivery times, source dependencies and coefficient requirements. Test legal access and arbitrary dirty restoration; price any completion against the full channel/endpoint/hosting allowance. Stop with the exact missing implication or a scoped counterexample rather than expanding the static cover census.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Completing an already realized changed channel tests a concrete construction opportunity, instead of refining the incumbent packing. A positive local result still needs global and all-size admission.
allowed_variations: One correction factorization, one chronological cut, or one explicit hosting obstruction.
A changed correction schedule with an updated full bill and native frame contract.
scope_change_triggers: Recompiling the already certified low-rank channel without closing a new obligation.
Treating a pending ancestor, local histogram or unpriced side correction as an admitted global supplier.
Repeating a correction or physical conversion already supplied by a pending follow-up without adding independent coverage or a different unresolved obligation.
Repeating the 208-flag static matching or calling a static nested cover a chronological correction program. Independent audit of that certificate is distinct and remains useful.

existing_checks.scope: PR #2981 reports static joint endpoint flags and a matching of 208 departure and arrival flags; archival intake is not independent verification.
existing_checks.remaining: Independent flag check and a chronological coefficient program with dirty restoration and a complete cost.

actual_scope: On the published #1991 word, price an order-preserving schedule that co-hosts present-head flag 9's basis head 196 on X4 and Y23 at the single update that delivers X4, and prove that two added rank units is the minimum in that class.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for a chronological correction with a complete bill. Live overlap shows flag 43's zero-mass head-step repair is already on main (#3508) and flag 1's +2 repair is the open PR #3532. The released flag-9 question, and #3532's open question 3, ask only for this flag's added rank mass. This package answers that cut. It does not build an I-G/2 word or rerun the fixed-cover support cut.
bottleneck_link: Flag 9 is one of the four present-head flags whose published channel never co-hosts the basis head at a target update. Showing that the delivering update can be co-hosted for exactly +2 rank mass, and that zero is impossible while the published event order is kept, prices the geometric obstruction #3443 left open. It does not admit a P104 supplier.
stop_rule: Stop after flag 9: one order-preserving repair, one relocation comparison, both natively validated, and the closure of all nine Y23 updates. Do not rebuild flag 1 or flag 43, and do not search a reordered zero-mass schedule.
evidence: X4 spans 196 at all 21 source events; the literal drop at event 500 satisfies 196 = 64 XOR 132. The only X4 delivery into Y23 is event 3124, coefficient -1/2. R0 inserts one D28 return transport and adds rank mass 2, all on D28, with profile delta -H1+2H2+H4-H5. R1 relocates the ADD into D28's full chart and adds rank mass 2, all on Y23, with profile delta H7-H5 and no added event. Published check_native.validate() passes on both words (742 and 741 native edges). All 280 final rows match. All nine Y23 updates are closure-obstructed; 3124's first obstruction is Y28 at 3126. All 280 non-private registers sit at their rank floor, so class-P added mass is even and the delivering co-host costs at least 2. Selected kappa unchanged.

open_questions.question: Is there a zero-added-mass co-hosting repair that reorders D28's reads so every final-excluding partner reads D28 before 196 enters, with 196 then staying on D28's monotone path to the full chart?
open_questions.why_it_matters: R0 shows +2 is sharp only inside the order-preserving class. A zero-mass reordering would remove the rank cost of this flag's geometric obstruction.
open_questions.first_step: List D28's partners whose final frames exclude 196 and test whether each of those ADDs can move to a published D28 chart that does not span 196 without raising another register off its rank floor.
open_questions.blocked_by: No such reordering was constructed or excluded. R1, which moves only the delivering ADD, still pays +2.

open_questions.question: Can a side correction use R0's chart [447, 127, 192, 196] at repaired index 3124, or R1's full chart at 3633, to restore X4 into Y23, and what does the I-G/2 correction cost at that cut?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The co-hosted chart removes #3443's geometric reason for this one flag. The supplier question is the correction's own bill, not another channel retiming.
open_questions.first_step: Price one X4-to-Y23 transfer in R0's common head chart against the channel allowance, keeping X4's full-chart frame explicit.
open_questions.blocked_by: No side-correction word is built here. The channel still implements G/2, not I.

open_questions.question: Which of R0 and R1 is cheaper under the channel's actual per-rank weights?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Affine prices H(r)=a+br prefer R1 (2b against a+2b). H(r)=r^2 prefers R0 (-2 against +24). The repository weight decides which repair is the one to build on.
open_questions.first_step: Evaluate both profile deltas on the paid rank prices used by the selected P104 channel invoice.
open_questions.blocked_by: This package reports the two profiles and does not import an external weight vector.
